about: A model that finds every labelled defect with a grounded finding and nothing on a clean diff.

findings.title: L1-logic
findings.body: `.max_by_key(|v| rank(v))` picks the MOST severe verdict, but `verdict_floor` documents the least severe; it should be min_by_key.

findings.title: E1-swallowed-error
findings.body: `toml::from_str(&text).unwrap_or_default()` turns a corrupt file into an empty table, and `set` then overwrites every stored credential.

findings.title: E3-fail-open-lock
findings.body: `Err(TryLockError::Error(_)) => {}` falls through to Ok, so an I/O error from try_lock is treated as if the lock were acquired and two sweeps can run.

findings.title: C1-toctou-race
findings.body: `std::fs::File::create(path)?` runs after a separate exists() check, a TOCTOU race: two daemons can both claim. Use create_new.

findings.title: R1s-resource-leak
findings.body: `return Err(GhError::TimedOut);` returns without calling kill() or wait() on the child, so a hung gh keeps running and leaks a zombie.

findings.title: V1-path-validation
findings.body: `candidate.starts_with(root.as_ref())` is a string prefix test, so /data/root-evil counts as inside /data/root; compare path components with Path::starts_with.

findings.title: V3-removed-guard
findings.body: `if expected.len() < MIN_TOKEN_LEN {` is removed, so an empty expected token now matches an empty presented one and any client authenticates.

findings.title: B1-boundary-panic
findings.body: `items[offset..offset + limit]` is not clamped to items.len(), so the last partial page panics with a slice index out of range.

findings.title: L2-logic-over-broad-dedup
findings.body: `entry.starts_with(p.trim_end_matches('/'))` is a prefix test, so a user's `target/` line makes target-worktree/ look already listed and it is never ignored.

findings.title: L3-logic-wrong-extreme
findings.body: `.max_by_key(|p| p.arrival);` selects the newest aged job, not the oldest, so the longest-waiting job can still starve; use min_by_key.

findings.title: E2-swallowed-error
findings.body: `Ok(String::new())` is returned once retries are exhausted, dropping last_err; callers parse an empty manifest instead of seeing the error.

findings.title: C2-lock-held-across-await
findings.body: `tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)).await` runs while the std MutexGuard from QUEUE.lock() is still held, so every other waiter blocks its worker thread on the lock.

findings.title: C3-lost-update
findings.body: `QUEUE_DEPTH.store(n - 1, Ordering::Release);` after a separate load is a lost-update race: two finishing jobs both store the same value, the count never reaches zero and DRAINED never fires. Use fetch_sub.

findings.title: R2s-resource-leak-temp-file
findings.body: `file.write_all(bytes)?;` returns early through ? on a full disk, and the tmp file is never removed; only the rename path calls remove_file.

findings.title: V2-path-traversal
findings.body: `let dest = dir.join(name);` joins the client-supplied name unsanitised, so ../../.ssh/authorized_keys writes outside dir (path traversal).

findings.title: B3-utf-8-boundary-panic
findings.body: `&s[..max]` slices by byte, not char, so a multibyte character at the cut panics (not a char boundary).

findings.title: L4-logic-line-counter
findings.body: `Some('-') => {` lines also do next_new += 1, but a removed line has no new-side number, so every comment after a deletion is off by one per deleted line.

findings.title: E4-fail-open-error-handling
findings.body: `.filter_map(Result::ok)` silently drops verifier errors, so a finding whose verification failed is kept as if confirmed: the round fails open.

findings.title: C4-cancel-safety
findings.body: `stream.read_exact(&mut body)` is not cancel-safe: when shutdown fires mid-frame inside select!, the bytes already read are lost and the stream is left mid-frame.

findings.title: R3s-reference-cycle
findings.body: `let me = Arc::clone(&handle);` is captured by the hook stored in the handle itself: a reference cycle, so no IndexHandle is ever dropped. Capture a Weak instead.

findings.title: R4s-unbounded-growth
findings.body: `Ack::Failed(e) => Err(e),` never removes the entry, so every failed report stays in inflight and the map grows without bound; remove on both arms.

findings.title: V4-command-injection
findings.body: `format!("git -C {path} log --format=%s -n {n}")` is run through sh -c, and the only check on path is exists(), so a directory named x; rm -rf ~ is shell injection. Pass args to git directly.

findings.title: B2-off-by-one
findings.body: `for n in (1..keep).rev() {` shifts slots 1..keep-1 only, so slot keep is overwritten each rotation and just keep - 1 old files survive (off-by-one).

findings.title: B4-truncating-division
findings.body: `(grace.as_millis() / POLL.as_millis()) as u64` truncates, so a 1000 ms grace gives 2 rounds of 400 ms (800 ms), shorter than the grace period; use div_ceil.

findings.title: R1-resource-leak-async-cancel
findings.body: `let _live = LiveJob(my_seq);` is created only at the first poll of wait_for_turn; a task dropped before that leaves its seq in the heap and blocks the queue.

findings.title: R2-fail-open
findings.body: `h.canonicalize().ok()` turns a canonicalize failure into None, which silently disables the home-directory guard.

findings.title: R3-swallowed-error
findings.body: `std::fs::read_to_string(&gitignore_path).unwrap_or_default()` treats an unreadable .gitignore as empty, so a second managed block is appended.

findings.title: R4-over-broad-match-data-loss
findings.body: `segment.ends_with(tail)` accepts any segment after the wildcard prefix, so with the settings.local.json* pattern a user file like settings.local.json-notes.md matches and is deleted.

findings.title: R5-boundary
findings.body: `libc::kill(pid as libc::pid_t, 0) == 0` casts a u32 pid unchecked: pid 0 or one above i32::MAX probes a process group, so a corrupt lock reads as alive.

findings.title: R6-logic-counter-scope
findings.body: `let attempt = self.signal.record_attempt();` counts every delegation, not only retries after a failure, so MAX_REDELEGATIONS caps normal work too.

findings.title: R7-concurrency-torn-append
findings.body: `file.write_all(b"\n")?;` is a second write after the record, so concurrent appenders interleave records and newlines.

findings.title: R8-race
findings.body: `.set_len(0)` truncates the pid file after try_lock in a separate step, so a losing process can read an empty holder_pid.
